advances: For the exact original log-affine height-lift family, the proposed vanishing typical-cap test has the opposite outcome: the original normalized actual depth tends to infinity in probability. In particular, no exposed-face cap construction, including an initial-path face followed by Boolean-coordinate fixes, can give the proposed vanishing upper bound at typical original roots. The third moments of this family tend to infinity after multiplication by \(8^N\), so this family does not refute the universal third-moment hypothesis. This conclusion uses an every-depth, disjoint-triple lower bound on actual closed caps, together with the original root-mass census. It makes no claim about the locked weak Oertel conjecture or the independently considered uniform depth-four family.
author: research-agent
external_sources: None. The complete tree support, level census, successor injectivity, symmetric-chain count, and central-binomial bound are used from 032423921efad6c8. The exact log-affine height lift, original weights, complete columns, and total-mass estimates are used from 604889294a17d7df. The disjoint-triple pattern in c2b7164e5a46e1b3 is extended to arbitrary original prefixes and checked explicitly in \(4\)-\(6\). The actual probability-depth and third-moment conventions, and the universal hypothesis being tested, are those of c3ede657c2f01110. All local witnesses, root-distribution estimates, and cap bounds are proved here without computational or external premises.
proof:
We first give the exact local witnesses. The following construction extends the disjoint triples in c2b7164e5a46e1b3, equation \(34\), to the unfixed Boolean subtree of an arbitrary level-\(s\) target. Its local labels \(p,q\) correspond here to \(i_V,i_U\), reserving \(p\) for the original probability law. All membership and cap claims are checked here.

Fix \(j\in A_{m,Q}\) of level \(s<Q\). Its twos form its initial path, by 032423921efad6c8. Let \(v\) be the last node of that path, or the empty root when \(s=0\). The coordinates below \(v\) are Boolean in \(j\). Suppose the Boolean child block \(j[v]\) has two successive predecessors in its chosen symmetric chain. There are then distinct labels \(i_V,i_U\in[m]\), both at coordinates where \(j[v]\) equals one, such that
\[
F_m(j[v]-e_{i_V})=j[v],\qquad
F_m(j[v]-e_{i_V}-e_{i_U})=j[v]-e_{i_V}.
\tag{4}
\]
Let \(r\ge1\) with \(s+r\le Q\). Start two paths at the distinct children
\[
U_1=vi_U,\qquad V_1=vi_V.
\]
Continue each path for \(r\) coordinates by taking the unique inverse-successor child of its Boolean target block whenever that block is in \(\operatorname{im}F_m\). Suppose all \(2(r-1)\) needed continuation blocks are in this image. Write their coordinates as \(U_i,V_i\), \(1\le i\le r\). The two paths lie in different child subtrees of \(v\), and every one of their target coordinates equals one.

For each \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_2,\ldots,\varepsilon_r)\in\{0,1\}^{r-1}\), define three full tree vectors \(x^{(1)}_\varepsilon,x^{(2)}_\varepsilon,x^{(3)}_\varepsilon\) by the following entries, leaving every unlisted coordinate equal to its value in \(j\):
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
\text{coordinate}&x^{(1)}_\varepsilon&x^{(2)}_\varepsilon&x^{(3)}_\varepsilon\\ \hline
U_1&2&1&0\\
V_1&0&2&1\\
U_i\ (2\le i\le r)&2&1-\varepsilon_i&\varepsilon_i\\
V_i\ (2\le i\le r)&1-\varepsilon_i&2&\varepsilon_i
\end{array}
\tag{5}
\]
Their average is exactly \(j\): each listed row sums to three, and each such coordinate of \(j\) equals one. The pre-existing prefix coordinates equal to two stay equal to two in all three vectors.

Replace all twos in \(x^{(1)}_\varepsilon\) by zeros to obtain its Boolean source. Its original first \(s\) successor choices remain valid because no modification has occurred in their determining child blocks. At \(v\), its block is \(j[v]-e_{i_V}-e_{i_U}\), so equation (4) selects \(i_U\). In every later visited block on the \(U\)-path, its block is exactly the unique predecessor of the corresponding block of \(j\). The modifications on the \(V\)-path are in the other child subtree and do not change those blocks. Thus its forward path goes through all \(U_1,\ldots,U_r\), and \(x^{(1)}_\varepsilon\in A_{m,Q}\) has level \(s+r\). The same argument for \(x^{(2)}_\varepsilon\), starting with the predecessor \(j[v]-e_{i_V}\), follows the \(V\)-path and gives level \(s+r\). The third vector has exactly the original prefix twos; its other coordinates are Boolean, and its modifications do not alter the first \(s\) determining blocks. Hence \(x^{(3)}_\varepsilon\in A_{m,Q}\) has level \(s\). This also checks that every source vector is complete on all tree coordinates.

Each family in \(5\) consists of \(2^{r-1}\) distinct vectors. In the first family the entries at \(V_2,\ldots,V_r\) recover \(\varepsilon\), and in the second and third families the entries at \(U_2,\ldots,U_r\) recover it. The three families are mutually disjoint because their sets of twos are the original prefix together with the \(U\)-path, the original prefix together with the \(V\)-path, and the original prefix alone. Thus \(5\) gives \(2^{r-1}\) triples with all source points distinct.

Now fix a lifted target \(\mathbf J=(j,t)\in\widehat A\). If \(a_{s+r}\le t\), lift all vectors in \(5\) to this same actual height \(t\). All these \(3\cdot2^{r-1}\) points belong to \(\widehat A\), all have their original weight \(2^{-t}\), and each triple has barycenter \(\mathbf J\). Every closed halfspace containing \(\mathbf J\) contains at least one source of every triple. Indeed, orient its affine defining functional to be nonnegative on the included side; if all three sources were excluded, all three values would be strictly negative, contradicting their average value at \(\mathbf J\). This counts equality atoms correctly. Disjointness consequently gives the actual cap bound
\[
W\tau_p(\mathbf J)\ge2^{r-1-t}.
\tag{6}
\]
No reflected-pair bound, conditional weight, continuous-fiber argument, or omitted height-column point enters \(6\). Other points of the full support can only add mass to each cap.

We next estimate how often the hypotheses of \(6\) hold under the original law. There are exactly \(2^n\eta^s\) level-\(s\) tree points, by 032423921efad6c8. Each is the image of exactly one Boolean source whose forward path has length at least \(s\). Conditional on level \(s\), that source is uniform among those sources. Condition further on its first \(s\) visited blocks and their path. Those child blocks are disjoint, their prescribed patterns belong to \(D_m\), and every unassigned Boolean coordinate is free. The entire descendant subtree of the last node \(v\) is therefore still a product of fair Boolean coordinates. Conditioning also on an allowed actual height \(t\) does not change this assertion, since every level-\(s\) point at that height has the same original weight \(2^{-t}\).

The symmetric-chain partition has exactly \(\binom m{m/2}=2^m\delta\) chains. At most two words in each chain lack two successive predecessors. Thus a uniform Boolean word has two predecessors with probability at least \(1-2\delta\). The image of \(F_m\) has cardinality \(2^m\eta\), so a fresh uniform Boolean block fails to be in that image with probability \(\delta\). After the first two predecessor steps have selected the distinct initial children in \(4\), the continuation reveals at most \(2(r-1)\) fresh, disjoint child blocks. Adaptive choice of a child does not change the fair distribution of its unvisited block. A union bound, conditional on any original prefix and allowed height, shows that the local hypotheses fail with probability at most
\[
2\delta+2(r-1)\delta=2r\delta.
\tag{7}
\]
This is valid for the specified recursive partition. Only its symmetric saturated-chain properties were needed.

For \(k\ge2^{13}\), define \(G_k\) as follows. A target \(\mathbf J=(j,t)\) belongs to \(G_k\) when its level \(s\ge1\) has entrance height \(\ell=a_s\ge L_k\),
\[
s\le Q_\ell-4\ell,\qquad t\le2\ell,
\tag{8}
\]
and its descendant Boolean subtree satisfies the local hypotheses above with \(r=4\ell\). Condition \(8\) implies \(s+r\le Q_\ell\le Q\) and \(a_{s+r}=\ell\le t\), so all lifted triples used in \(6\) are present at the actual height \(t\). Hence
\[
2^N\tau_p(\mathbf J)
\ge\frac{2^{4\ell-1-t}}{W/2^N}
\ge\frac{2^{2\ell-1}}{W/2^N}
\ge\frac{k^2}{2(W/2^N)}.
\tag{9}
\]
The last step uses \(2^{L_k}\ge k\). The upper mass bound \(W/2^N\le1+(H_k-H_7)/8\) from 604889294a17d7df now proves \(2\).

For the mass of the excluded roots, use the exact census
\[
\mathbb P_p\{\operatorname{lev}(j)=s,\ t=h\}
=\frac{2^n\eta^s2^{-h}}{W}
\quad(a_s\le h\le k).
\tag{10}
\]
All estimates below sum actual weights over complete height columns and then divide by \(W\). Removing a factor \(\eta^s\le1\) only increases each upper bound.

The original weight of the Boolean level and of levels with entrance height below \(L_k\), divided by \(2^n\), is at most
\[
\sum_{t=0}^k2^{-t}
+\sum_{\ell=8}^{L_k-1}b_\ell\sum_{t=\ell}^k2^{-t}
\le2+\frac{H_{L_k-1}-H_7}{4}.
\tag{11}
\]
Here \(b_\ell\le2^\ell/(8\ell)\) and each height tail is at most \(2^{1-\ell}\). In the entrance block for \(\ell\), at most \(4\ell\) levels violate \(s\le Q_\ell-4\ell\), even when the whole block has fewer levels. Their combined original weight, divided by \(2^n\), is at most
\[
\sum_{\ell=8}^k4\ell\,2^{1-\ell}
\le8\sum_{\ell=8}^{\infty}\ell2^{-\ell}
=\frac9{16}.
\tag{12}
\]
For levels with entrance height \(\ell\ge8\), the original weight of heights \(t>2\ell\), divided by \(2^n\), is at most
\[
\sum_{\ell=8}^kb_\ell\sum_{t=2\ell+1}^k2^{-t}
\le\sum_{\ell=8}^{\infty}\frac{2^{-\ell}}{8\ell}
\le\frac1{8192}.
\tag{13}
\]
The last inequality uses \(\ell\ge8\) and \(\sum_{\ell=8}^{\infty}2^{-\ell}=1/128\); an empty finite height tail contributes zero. Finally, on any level and height satisfying \(8\), \(7\) with \(r=4\ell\le4k\) bounds the conditional failure probability by \(8k\delta\). Accepted fact 032423921efad6c8 gives, for this exact \(m\),
\[
0<\delta<\frac1{(Q+1)^2}.
\tag{14}
\]
Combining \(11\)-\(14\) by a union bound, and using \(W/2^n=2(W/2^N)\), proves \(3\).

To check its limit directly, 604889294a17d7df gives \(W/2^N\sim H_k/8\). The numerator involving \(L_k\) in \(3\) grows at most as \(\log L_k\), whereas \(H_k\ge\log(k+1)\) and \(L_k=\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\). Thus that quotient tends to zero. Also \(Q\ge b_k=\lfloor2^k/(8k)\rfloor\), so \(8k/(Q+1)^2\to0\). Therefore \(p(G_k)\to1\). The bound in \(2\) tends to infinity, since \(H_k\le1+\log k\). This proves the probability assertion in \(1\). In the unchanged moment normalization of c3ede657c2f01110,
\[
8^NM_3(p)=\mathbb E_p[(2^N\tau_p(\mathbf J))^3]
\ge p(G_k)
\left(\frac{k^2}{2(1+(H_k-H_7)/8)}\right)^3
\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{15}
\]
No uniform-integrability premise is needed for this lower bound. It establishes the opposite of the proposed vanishing third moment.

For a quantitative reconciliation with the specially constructed deep roots, the all-ones tree target has two predecessors in its root chain, and its inverse path continues at every later all-ones block. The local construction \(5\) with \(s=0,r=Q,t=k\) therefore gives
\[
W\tau_p((\mathbf1,k))\ge2^{Q-1-k}\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{16}
\]
This is also the direct discrete cap consequence of the disjoint triples in c2b7164e5a46e1b3. On the other hand, the entire original all-ones height column has probability
\[
p\{(\mathbf1,t):0\le t\le k\}
=\frac{\sum_{t=0}^k2^{-t}}W\le\frac2W\longrightarrow0.
\tag{17}
\]
Thus its large maximum depth and its small root mass are compatible. Equations \(3\) and \(9\) establish the relevant stronger conclusion: the same actual-cap obstruction occurs at a set of original roots whose total mass tends to one. Discarding the all-ones column would not remove it.

An exposed face containing \(\mathbf J\) must retain every source in every triple in \(5\): its exposing functional is maximized at their average, so the three individual values, each at most that maximum, must all equal the maximum. The same argument applies inductively to a sequence of exposed faces retaining \(\mathbf J\). Thus fixing the initial twos and then making permissible Boolean-coordinate face fixes cannot discard these sources. Every cap obtained by extending a face normal is still a closed halfspace containing its original target, and its trace must meet every one of the retained, disjoint, same-height triples. Equations \(6\) and \(9\) consequently obstruct both the face restriction and the eventual cap. This obstruction is independent of any growth of a fixed-depth coefficient bound. The result concerns this exact original log-affine support and law, and neither refutes the universal hypothesis in c3ede657c2f01110 nor furnishes an upper bound on any actual mixed-integer body's depth.
statement:
For each integer \(k\ge8\), take precisely the log-affine specialization of accepted fact 604889294a17d7df:
\[
\rho_t=2^{-t},\qquad
b_\ell=0\ (1\le\ell<8),\qquad
b_\ell=\left\lfloor\frac{2^\ell}{8\ell}\right\rfloor\ (8\le\ell\le k),
\qquad Q_\ell=\sum_{h=1}^{\ell}b_h,\quad Q=Q_k.
\]
Put \(a_0=0\), and \(a_s=\ell\) when \(Q_{\ell-1}<s\le Q_\ell\). Use the exact rooted-tree support of 032423921efad6c8 with \(m=2(Q+1)^4\), tree depth \(Q\), and its recursive symmetric-chain partition, with coordinates adjoined in the order \(1,\ldots,m\). Write
\[
n=\sum_{h=1}^Qm^h,\qquad N=n+1,\qquad
\eta=1-\delta,\qquad \delta=2^{-m}\binom m{m/2},
\]
\[
\widehat A=\{(z,t):z\in A_{m,Q},\ a_{\operatorname{lev}(z)}\le t\le k,\ t\in\mathbb Z\},
\qquad w_{(z,t)}=2^{-t},\qquad
W=\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A}w_{\mathbf I},\qquad
p_{\mathbf I}=w_{\mathbf I}/W.
\]
Here \(\operatorname{lev}(z)\) is the number of coordinates of \(z\) equal to two, and \(H_h=\sum_{\ell=1}^h1/\ell\) for each positive integer \(h\).
The support is the complete, full-dimensional support in \(\mathbb Z^N\) from 604889294a17d7df. This is the original log-affine law on the entire lifted support, with exponential parameter \((0,\ldots,0,-\log2)\).

Use the actual depth and third moment of c3ede657c2f01110:
\[
\tau_p(\mathbf J)=\min_{\substack{H\text{ a closed halfspace}\\\mathbf J\in H}}
\sum_{\mathbf I\in\widehat A\cap H}p_{\mathbf I},
\qquad M_3(p)=\sum_{\mathbf J\in\widehat A}p_{\mathbf J}\tau_p(\mathbf J)^3.
\]
In that predecessor, its ambient dimension is here \(N\), its support \(D\) is here \(\widehat A\), and its exponential parameter is the vector just given; the present \(m\) is only the branching factor. In c2b7164e5a46e1b3, the tree dimension \(n_{\mathrm{tree}}\), height cutoff \(T\), common scale \(\omega\), and lifted support \(D\) correspond respectively to \(n,k,1,\widehat A\). The depth remains that of the original law \(p\); no conditional face law is used.

For \(\mathbf J\) sampled from \(p\), one has
\[
2^N\tau_p(\mathbf J)\longrightarrow\infty
\quad\text{in probability as }k\longrightarrow\infty,
\qquad
8^N M_3(p)\longrightarrow\infty.
\tag{1}
\]
An explicit high-probability witness is as follows. For \(k\ge2^{13}\), put \(L_k=\lceil\log_2 k\rceil\). There is a set \(G_k\subseteq\widehat A\) such that every \(\mathbf J\in G_k\) satisfies
\[
2^N\tau_p(\mathbf J)
\ge\frac{k^2}{2\left(1+(H_k-H_7)/8\right)},
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
p(G_k)\ge
1-
\frac{2+(H_{L_k-1}-H_7)/4+9/16+1/8192}
{2(W/2^N)}
-\frac{8k}{(Q+1)^2}.
\tag{3}
\]
The right side tends to one. In particular, for every fixed \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
\mathbb P_p\{2^N\tau_p(\mathbf J)\ge\epsilon\}\longrightarrow1,
\]
which rules out the vanishing-probability upper-cap test in the registered subgoal.
